# Clinical Assessment

This folder contains clinical assessment and scoring systems used to stratify risk, predict mortality, and evaluate patient severity in the context of acute surgery. These scores range from general anesthesia and intensive care metrics, like the ASA classification and APACHE, to procedure-specific tools like the PULP-score for perforated ulcers. The database evaluates several of these instruments to determine their practical utility for quality indicators, often favoring simpler demographic and comorbidity thresholds over complex perioperative scoring models.

## Pages

- [[apache|APACHE]] — Intensive care scoring system evaluated for pre-operative mortality prediction but deemed too comprehensive for routine practical use.
- [[asa-score|ASA]] — Anesthesia physical status classification where a score of ≥ 3 identifies high-risk patients requiring extended postoperative monitoring.
- [[charlson-score-ge-3|Charlson Score ≥ 3]] — Threshold indicating high registered comorbidity, used as a supplementary indicator for 30-day postoperative mortality.
- [[p-possum|P-POSSUM]] — Post-operative risk scoring system incorporating pre- and intra-operative variables, considered too extensive for everyday clinical application.
- [[pulp-score|PULP-score]] — Prognostic tool specifically designed to predict mortality in patients with perforated peptic ulcers.
- [[surgical-apgar-score|Surgical Apgar Score]] — Intra-operative scoring metric criticized for potentially excluding high-risk patients who do not exhibit physiological stress during surgery.
